segments.he:
בעת שהי' רבינו ז"ל בימי נעוריו והי' מתענה משבת לשבת ופעם אחד באמצע השבוע לא הי' יכול להשלים התענית והי' סכנת נפשות ואמר ר' חייקיל החזן של רבינו ז"ל שיעשה לו תרנגולת לאכילה ופעל אצלו והלך ר' חייקיל תיכף ושחט תרנגולת ועל הדרך מרט את הנוצות והכשירה ובשלה והביא את המרק לפני רבינו ז"ל והי' בליל ד' בתחלת הלילה וכשהביא לרבינו ז"ל המרק והאוכל ענה רבינו ז"ל ואמר לו זמר מעין עולם הבא (חייקיר זינג מעין עוה"ב) 
(בזה הניגון הידוע לנו) וזמר מעין עוה"ב וכשגמר ורצה שרבינו יאכל כבר השיב לו שיזמר עוד וכן זמר כל הלילה והאוכל בידו ורבינו התעמק בהניגון עד שהגיע זמן ק"ש של שחרית ולא הפסיק תעניתו עד שבת כמנהגו:
segments.en:
My father told me that he knew a man who had a companion who had mastered the art of ve-choiver chaver — a charmer who could gather serpents with his incantations. Both were genuinely G-d-fearing men. Once the companion offered to show him something remarkable in a field. He positioned him on a tree on a hillside and went down to the open valley — and began to mutter with his lips. Suddenly from all four directions of the world came enormous and terrible serpents in caravan after caravan — like beams from an olive-press — and they surrounded the charmer. The observer on the tree was seized with absolute terror — fear of death.

Suddenly he heard his companion cry out: "Gevald! Ikh bin farloyrn!" [Help! I am lost!] He called from the tree: "Why?" He replied: "There is a serpent called the Pasan Cheresh — a deaf snake with only one ear that hears. It suffers greatly when called and must come — therefore it always goes and presses its hearing ear into the ground so as not to hear the charmer. But when its ear is not stopped and it hears and is compelled to come — the charmer is destroyed. Now I feel my bad fortune that its ear was not stopped and it heard my call — and therefore I am lost." He cried out Shema Yisroel. From the tree the observer saw the most terrible of all those serpents approaching the man — and it did nothing to him except blow into his face. And then it was gone — and all the snakes departed. He climbed down from the tree — and could find no trace of his companion except a small amount of burnt ash and dust. He gathered it into a cloth, wept over him, brought it home, and buried it. When the companion had described the Pasan Cheresh, he also said this is alluded to in Tehillim 58: "Pasan cheresh — ye'atem ozno" — a deaf snake who stops up its [hearing] ear. The apparent difficulty — if it is deaf, why does it stop up its ear? — is answered: it is deaf in only one ear, and the ear it does hear with, it stops up so as not to hear the charmer. May Hashem protect us.
